title: Shader Skins, Drawing Sheets, Glyph Clusters, CSS Springs & Document Links
description: Shader layers over live HTML, a component as a technical sheet, type moved cluster by cluster, springs declared in CSS, docs in the URL.

drops.title: A Shader Over Live HTML
drops.description: Three real cards captured into GPU textures and re-drawn through ripple, lens and dither shaders — with the live DOM one click away.
drops.concept: Canvas UI's idea is that the effect layer sits on top of the actual interface rather than replacing it: the subtree is captured (natively with HTML-in-canvas drawElement, or via an SVG foreignObject snapshot), uploaded with texImage2D and distorted by a fragment shader while the real markup stays selectable underneath. Each panel here runs a different shader off the same capture, and the pointer pushes the fluid around. It is hot because it finally makes shader polish composable with ordinary, accessible HTML.
drops.source: DavidHDev/canvas-ui — creative canvas components, WebGL effects over real HTML

interaction.mouse: Move over a panel to displace the ripple or drag the lens around; the glow follows the pointer.
interaction.click: The pill in each footer flips that panel between the shader layer and the live HTML; the panel re-snapshots on demand.
interaction.touch: Drag across a panel — pointer events drive the same uniforms.

drops.title: The Component as a Technical Drawing
drops.description: A plan view with hatched padding and dimensioned radii, an exploded layer stack you can orbit, and a table of relationships.
drops.concept: Apple's accessory dimensional drawings describe an object's architecture, not its content, and this project applies that to UI components: paddings, radii, layer order and roles — FLEX, HUG, FILL — in grayscale, with variables like H1 = 2·S1 + H3 instead of magic numbers. The drawing is generated from a small spec, so switching from a card to a dialog to a switch redraws the sheet. It reads as documentation a designer and an engineer can both sign off.
drops.source: enesozturk/dimensional-drawing — Apple-style dimensional drawings of UI components

interaction.mouse: Drag the exploded view to orbit it; hover a layer to light its row in the variable table.
interaction.click: The chips switch subject — card, dialog, switch — and the panel collapses the stack back to a plan or swaps to blueprint ink.
interaction.touch: The orbit drag is pointer-based; the sheet stacks to one column on narrow screens.

drops.title: Type, by the Cluster
drops.description: An astronaut emoji is one cluster and three code points. Canvas text split into graphemes, each with its own box, wave and shove.
drops.concept: Chrome 159 adds selection rectangles, bounding-box queries and glyph-cluster operations to Canvas TextMetrics — the pieces you need to animate or edit canvas text without guessing where a glyph ends. This demo segments three lines with Intl.Segmenter, measures each cluster, and moves them independently: a wave, a scatter and a cascade, plus a pointer that shoves clusters aside. The counters make the point that UTF-16 units, code points and clusters are three different numbers.
drops.source: Chrome 159 release notes — enhanced Canvas TextMetrics

interaction.mouse: Sweep a line to push clusters out of the way; rest on one to see its selection box and code points.
interaction.click: The panel cycles the motion assigned to each line and hides the cluster boxes.
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the canvas — the same pointer handler drives the push.

drops.title: Motion, Declared in CSS
drops.description: Elements ask for --k-tilt, --k-magnetic, --k-repel or --k-drag; one spring loop writes --k-x and friends back as typed custom properties.
drops.concept: Kinesis turns pointer motion into CSS custom properties: you declare the intent on the element and the library writes spring-animated values back, so every visual decision — glow, shadow, scale, colour — stays in the stylesheet. Registering the outputs with @property makes them real lengths and angles rather than strings. Here 46 elements share one loop that parks itself when nothing is moving, keyboard focus mirrors hover, and prefers-reduced-motion holds the springs at rest.
drops.source: amineyarman/Kinesis.js — interactive motion written in CSS

interaction.mouse: Approach the cards to tilt them, the buttons to make them lean, the dot grid to scatter it.
interaction.click: Grab a chip and throw it — the same spring carries the overshoot home; the panel tunes stiffness, damping, strength and radius.
interaction.touch: Chips are draggable with touch-action: none; the hover-driven groups stay still, as they should.

drops.title: The Document Inside the Link
drops.description: A note, a checklist and a sheet whose only storage is the URL fragment — deflated and base64url-packed as you type.
drops.concept: Tiny Little Office's premise is that the document is the link: everything you type lives in the fragment after the #, the part a browser never sends to a server, so there is no account, no save button and nothing to delete. These three mini documents serialise through CompressionStream('deflate-raw') into base64url and rewrite the address bar on every keystroke, with a meter showing how much of a comfortable link budget each one has eaten. Paste a link back in and the documents return.
drops.source: aboard-io/tinylittleoffice — a free office suite where the document is inside the link

interaction.mouse: Type in the note, tick the checklist, edit a sheet cell and watch the totals and the link length update.
interaction.click: Copy a document's own link, narrow the address bar to one document, or paste someone else's link and load it.
interaction.touch: Everything is a native control — textarea, checkbox, contenteditable — so touch editing works as usual.
